champion.challengeFraming: Name the exact manual process and the role of the person doing it. For Homage: adapt to migration context — the pain is not end-user data entry but operational brittleness: Sikich managing Celigo day-to-day, ~23 flows maintained via custom JS hooks that only Sikich understands, a Turbine middleware no one fully owns, and an EDI track running outside the integration platform entirely. Frame: 'Your current integration infrastructure is maintainable only through your NetSuite partner — that dependency ends on go-live day.'
champion.fomoFraming: Lead with hours saved and the specific manual task that disappears. Structure: '{X hours/week} recovered — {the exact task} is gone on go-live day.' For Homage: the 'task that disappears' is Sikich's Celigo maintenance overhead and ad-hoc custom JS fixes — each one a risk event that stops.
champion.journeyFraming: Stage 1 bullet items should read like a 'things that stop happening Monday morning' list. Use active verbs: 'stops,' 'disappears,' 'no longer.' Stage 2 gets two sentences. Stage 3 gets one — plant the seed without over-pitching to someone who wants immediate relief.
champion.closingLineVariant: Stage 1 eliminates the specific manual work your team does today. Stages 2 and 3 build on that foundation — but the immediate win is on go-live day.

economicBuyer.executiveSummaryFraming: Open with what stops on go-live day — name the specific operational dependencies that disappear (Sikich maintaining 23 Celigo flows, custom JS upkeep, Turbine middleware). Lead with: 'Your current integration infrastructure depends on a third party to stay running — that dependency ends at go-live.'
